title: Rice blast (Magnaporthe oryzae)
body: Diamond-shaped grey lesions with brown margins on leaves; can girdle the neck of the panicle. Spray tricyclazole (0.6g/L) at first sign, avoid excess nitrogen, use resistant varieties where available.

title: Yellow/stripe rust in wheat
body: Yellow powdery stripes on leaves in cool, humid weather. Spray Propiconazole 25EC (1ml/L) at the first sign; sow rust-resistant varieties (HD-3086, DBW-187) in endemic belts.

title: Pink bollworm in cotton
body: Look for rosette flowers and pin-holed bolls. Install pheromone traps (5/acre), hand-pick infested bolls, spray profenofos only if 8 moths/trap/night threshold is crossed.

title: Aphid management
body: Sticky honeydew and curled leaves signal aphids. Release ladybird beetles, spray neem oil (5ml/L) weekly, or use imidacloprid 17.8SL (0.3ml/L) only if infestation is severe.

title: Stem borer control
body: Dead hearts in vegetative stage or white earheads later indicate stem borer. Use pheromone traps, apply cartap hydrochloride 4G at 20kg/acre in standing water.

title: Red rot in sugarcane
body: Reddening inside the stalk with a sour smell indicates red rot. Use disease-free setts, hot water seed treatment (52°C for 30 min), and resistant varieties.

title: NPK fertilizer basics
body: Nitrogen drives leafy growth, phosphorus roots/flowering, potassium overall vigour and disease resistance. Split nitrogen into 2-3 doses; base the exact dose on your Soil Health Card.

title: Micronutrient deficiency symptoms
body: Zinc deficiency shows as interveinal yellowing/bronzing in rice; boron deficiency causes poor flowering/fruit-set in cauliflower and fruit crops. Apply zinc sulphate (25kg/ha) or borax as per soil test.

title: Biofertilizers
body: Rhizobium culture for legumes, Azotobacter for cereals, and Phosphate Solubilising Bacteria (PSB) reduce chemical fertilizer need by 15-20%. Treat seed just before sowing, keep in shade, avoid mixing with chemical fungicide directly.

title: Soil Health Card Scheme
body: Free government soil testing every 2 years giving crop-wise nutrient recommendations. Apply through your nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra or Krishibhavan; results take 2-3 weeks.

title: PM-KISAN income support
body: ₹6,000/year paid in three ₹2,000 installments directly to eligible small/marginal farmer bank accounts. Check status at the PM-KISAN portal or nearest Common Service Centre.

title: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana
body: Subsidised crop insurance against yield loss from calamities, pests, and disease. Report crop damage to the insurer/bank within 72 hours; premium capped at 1.5-5% of sum insured.

title: Kisan Credit Card
body: Short-term credit up to ₹3 lakh at subsidised interest (~4% with prompt repayment) for crop and allied needs. Apply at any nationalised bank/RRB with land records and Aadhaar.

title: PM-KUSUM solar pump subsidy
body: Up to 60% subsidy (30% central + 30% state) on standalone solar irrigation pumps, with an additional 30% bank loan available. Apply through the state renewable energy agency portal.

title: Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO) support
body: Groups of 300+ (plains) or 100+ (hilly) farmers can register an FPO to access collective input purchase, better market linkage, and government matching equity grants up to ₹15 lakh.

title: Custom Hiring Centres & machinery subsidy
body: Farmers can rent tractors, harvesters, and implements at subsidised rates from Custom Hiring Centres set up under the Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization, cutting individual capital cost.

title: Drip & sprinkler irrigation
body: Drip can cut water use by 30-50% and boost yield for row crops. Subsidy up to 55% available under PMKSY - Per Drop More Crop; apply via the state horticulture department.

title: Irrigation scheduling basics
body: Irrigate at critical growth stages (tillering, flowering, grain-fill) rather than fixed calendar days. Check soil moisture at 15cm depth by hand — irrigate when it no longer forms a ball.

title: Farm ponds & water harvesting
body: A lined farm pond of 20x20x3m can store enough water for 1-2 protective irrigations on 2-3 acres. Subsidy available under MGNREGA and state watershed programmes for construction.

title: Fertigation through drip
body: Applying water-soluble fertilizer through the drip system improves nutrient use efficiency by 25-30% versus soil application. Inject in the second half of each irrigation cycle, never at the very start or end.

title: On-farm composting & natural inputs
body: Vermicompost and Jeevamrut (cow dung + urine + jaggery + gram flour, fermented 7 days) build soil biology. Apply Jeevamrut diluted 1:10 with irrigation water every 15 days.

title: Biopesticides & neem-based sprays
body: Neem seed kernel extract (5%) and Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) sprays control caterpillar pests with minimal impact on beneficial insects; spray in the evening for best effect.

title: Mulching for moisture & weed control
body: Straw or black plastic mulch cuts soil moisture loss by up to 40% and suppresses weeds, especially valuable for vegetables and drip-irrigated crops.

title: Seed treatment before sowing
body: Treat seed with Trichoderma viride (4g/kg) or carbendazim to control soil-borne disease. Use certified seed and the recommended seed rate for your variety and spacing.

title: SRI & direct-seeded rice
body: System of Rice Intensification (young single seedlings, wide spacing, alternate wetting-drying) can cut seed and water use by 30-40% while raising yield. Direct-seeded rice further reduces labour for transplanting.

title: Zero tillage wheat sowing
body: Sowing wheat directly into rice stubble with a Happy Seeder avoids stubble burning, saves 25-30% on cultivation cost, and improves soil organic matter over seasons.

title: Intercropping & rotation
body: Rotating cereals with legumes fixes nitrogen and breaks pest/disease cycles. Intercropping (e.g., cotton + moong) spreads risk and improves per-acre returns.

title: Weed management
body: Apply pre-emergence herbicide (e.g., pendimethalin) within 2-3 days of sowing, followed by one hand-weeding at 25-30 days for best results; rotate herbicide groups to avoid resistance.

title: Managing soil pH
body: Most field crops prefer pH 6-7.5. For acidic soils apply agricultural lime per your Soil Health Card dose; for alkaline/saline soils apply gypsum and improve drainage.

title: Soil erosion control
body: Contour bunding, vegetative barriers (vetiver grass), and terracing on sloped land can cut soil loss by over 50% and retain more rainwater on the field.

title: Weather-linked farm advisory
body: Delay spraying/fertilizer if rain is forecast within 24 hours to avoid wash-off. For heatwaves irrigate early morning/evening; for frost risk, light smoke or irrigation before dawn protects tender crops.

title: Managing drought/dry spells
body: Apply a light protective irrigation at the most critical growth stage if only one is available, mulch to conserve moisture, and consider short-duration, drought-tolerant varieties in delayed-monsoon years.

title: Managing waterlogging/flood damage
body: Drain excess water within 48 hours where possible, avoid fertilizer application until the field dries, and monitor for fungal disease which spikes after waterlogging.

title: Mandi prices & MSP
body: Check live mandi rates on the e-NAM portal or Agmarknet before selling. If the mandi price is below MSP for a notified crop, sell through government procurement centres instead.

title: Warehouse receipt financing
body: Store produce in a registered warehouse and pledge the e-NWR (electronic Negotiable Warehouse Receipt) to get a loan up to 70-80% of commodity value, avoiding distress sale right after harvest.

title: Contract farming basics
body: A written pre-agreed price and buyback agreement with a company reduces price risk but check quality clauses and payment terms carefully before signing; local Krishibhavan can help review terms.

title: Post-harvest storage
body: Dry grain to below 12% moisture before storage, use hermetic (airtight) bags or metal bins to prevent pest damage, and consider registered warehouses instead of distress selling.

title: Grading, packaging & value addition
body: Sorting and grading produce by size/quality can fetch 10-20% higher prices; simple value addition (e.g., turmeric powder, tomato puree) further improves margins over selling raw produce.

title: Fall armyworm in maize
body: Look for window-pane feeding on young leaves and larvae in the whorl. Apply emamectin benzoate 5SG (0.4g/L) directly into the whorl in the early morning or evening for best control.

title: Tikka leaf spot in groundnut
body: Circular brown/black spots with yellow halo on leaves. Spray chlorothalonil or mancozeb (2g/L) at 15-day intervals starting 30-35 days after sowing in a wet season.

title: Fusarium wilt in tur/arhar
body: Sudden wilting with yellowing, usually near flowering. Use wilt-resistant varieties, treat seed with Trichoderma, and avoid continuous tur cultivation on the same plot.

title: Aphid management in mustard
body: Check the terminal shoot and flowering branches for aphid colonies. Spray dimethoate or use yellow sticky traps; early sowing helps the crop escape peak aphid buildup.

title: Late blight in potato
body: Water-soaked lesions turning brown/black on leaves in cool, humid weather. Spray mancozeb preventively and switch to cymoxanil+mancozeb once disease appears; avoid overhead irrigation in humid spells.

title: Fruit borer in tomato
body: Pin-holes on fruit with larvae feeding inside indicate fruit borer. Use pheromone traps, remove and destroy damaged fruit, and spray spinosad if infestation crosses threshold.

title: Thrips in onion
body: Silvery streaks and curled leaf tips indicate thrips. Spray fipronil or a neem-based product, and avoid excess nitrogen which encourages thrips buildup.

title: Chilli leaf curl virus
body: Upward curling and puckering of leaves, transmitted by whitefly. Control whitefly with yellow sticky traps and imidacloprid seedling dip; remove and destroy infected plants early.

title: Mango flowering & fruit-drop management
body: Spray potassium nitrate (1%) to induce uniform flowering, and NAA (20ppm) at pea stage to reduce fruit drop. Avoid nitrogen fertilizer close to the flowering period.

title: Banana nutrition & bunch management
body: Apply NPK in split doses through fertigation for best bunch weight; remove the male bud after fruit set and prop plants before bunching to prevent lodging in wind.

title: Polyhouse/greenhouse subsidy
body: Up to 50-65% capital subsidy for polyhouse/shade-net structures under National Horticulture Mission, enabling off-season vegetable and flower cultivation with better pest control.

title: Agri-drone subsidy for spraying
body: Subsidy up to 40-50% (higher for FPOs and women farmers) on drones for pesticide/nutrient spraying, cutting spraying time and chemical drift compared to manual knapsack sprayers.

title: Kisan Call Centre helpline
body: Call the toll-free Kisan Call Centre (1800-180-1551) in your local language for advisory from agriculture graduates, available across most states from 6am to 10pm.

title: mKisan SMS advisory
body: Register on the mKisan portal to receive free SMS advisories in your language on weather, pest alerts, and market prices relevant to your district and crop.

title: Honeybee pollination benefits
body: Placing 4-5 bee colonies per acre during flowering can raise yield by 15-40% in crops like mustard, sunflower, and fruit orchards, alongside honey as an added income source.

title: Agroforestry & boundary plantation
body: Planting fast-growing trees (poplar, eucalyptus, or fruit trees) on field boundaries adds a long-term income stream and reduces wind erosion without significantly reducing main-crop yield.

title: Climate-resilient crop varieties
body: Short-duration and stress-tolerant varieties (e.g., Sahbhagi Dhan for drought, DRR Dhan 44 for submergence) help maintain yield stability under erratic monsoon patterns.
